title: Charlie Rouse mesmerized by Parker; Gene Ammons takes the chair
summary: Rouse stares at Parker's solos and misses his entrances, so Eckstine replaces him with Gene Ammons.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: A funny thing happened with Charlie during those weeks that he was there. The band used to play a certain number that Charlie Parker would have a solo in, and Charlie had a way that he would go up to the mike, play his solo, and as he was winding it up, it seemed like he could always time it perfectly. He would back up, and just as he would hit his

last note, he would be sitting down in his chair, and back to playing with his section. When this would happen, while Charlie Parker was playing his solo, Charlie Rouse would be so mesmerized by Charlie's playing that... Because when Charlie was playing the solo, the saxes aren't playing, so Charlie Rouse is just sitting there watching Charlie Parker!

So it got so that after the solo was over, and Charlie Parker is back in the section and the section is playing, Charlie Rouse would still be sitting there with his horn across his lap, looking at the mike where Charlie Parker had played, and we would be into another chorus, the sax section is playing and everything, and Billy would tell Charlie Rouse, he'd snap his fingers, "Come on, man! Come on! Come on!" And Charlie would come to himself, grab his horn, and start playing with the section. This went on for a number of nights.

So Billy came to me, and said "John, I'm sorry, but I'm going to have to let Charlie Rouse go, because he's not ready for this." "What's the matter?" "I don't know what it is, but he just can't keep his mind on what he's doing." Anyway, finally they sent and got Gene Ammons, or they alerted him... I think he joined us later -- I believe it was in Dayton, Ohio, that Gene Ammons joined us. Gene Ammons took Charlie Rouse's place.
